name: MonarchAiSourceList
title: AiSourceList
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.foundation.layout.Column of clickable source rows with MonarchFavicon, and a MonarchButton toggle; androidx.compose.ui.platform.LocalUriHandler opens links
summary: The block of sources under an AI answer: each with its favicon, [n] number, title, host, product, kind and snippet, grouped into Used and Considered, and collapsed to the first few.
whenToUse: Under an assistant reply that cites sources, so people can see and open what the answer is based on, in the same numbering as the citation markers in the text.
whenNotToUse: For one citation inside the text use MonarchAiCitation. For a preview of one source with the quoted passage use MonarchAiSourcePreview. For a list of links that are not AI sources use MonarchLinkCard or a plain list.
api: @Composable fun MonarchAiSourceList(items: List<MonarchAiSourceListItem>, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, collapseAfter: Int? = 3, initiallyExpanded: Boolean = false, numbered: Boolean = true, favicon: (@Composable (MonarchAiSourcePart) -> Painter?)? = null, labels: MonarchAiSourceListLabels = MonarchAiSourceListLabels(), onOpen: ((MonarchAiSourceListItem) -> Unit)? = null)

data class MonarchAiSourceListItem(source: MonarchAiSourcePart, used: Boolean = true, snippet: String? = null) { val id: String; companion object { fun sources(message: MonarchAiConversationMessage): List<MonarchAiSourceListItem> } }

class MonarchAiSourceListLabels(heading: String? = null, used: ((count: Int) -> String)? = null, considered: ((count: Int) -> String)? = null, showAll: ((count: Int) -> String)? = null, showFewer: String? = null, source: ((number: Int, title: String) -> String)? = null, openSource: String? = null, kind: ((kind: MonarchAiSourceKind) -> String)? = null)

options.name: items
options.description: The sources in citation order; the first is [1]. Each wraps the conversation model's MonarchAiSourcePart with used and a snippet.

options.name: collapseAfter
options.description: How many sources show while collapsed. null never collapses.

options.name: initiallyExpanded
options.description: Whether a collapsible list starts expanded.

options.name: numbered
options.description: Shows the [n] number that matches each source's citation marker.

options.name: favicon
options.description: The favicon the app loaded for a source; null shows MonarchFavicon's letter tile. Monarch loads no images.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for the heading, group headings, toggle titles, spoken source name, tap action name and kind names.

options.name: onOpen
options.description: Makes each source a button that calls this, for example to show MonarchAiSourcePreview. Without it, safe addresses open through LocalUriHandler.

states.name: ungrouped
states.description: All sources are used: one list under the heading.

states.name: grouped
states.description: Some sources were considered but not used: Used (n) and Considered (n) groups, used first.

states.name: collapsed
states.description: More sources than collapseAfter: the first few of used then considered show, with Show all n sources.

states.name: expanded
states.description: Every source shows, with Show fewer.

states.name: actionable
states.description: With onOpen each row is a button; otherwise a row with a safe address opens it and its title uses the link color.

states.name: plain
states.description: A source without onOpen and without a safe address is text in the default color.

appearance: The heading and group headings are muted text; titles use the link color when the row opens and default text otherwise; the [n] number, the meta line and the two-line snippet are muted. The favicon is MonarchFavicon at its small size, with its letter tile when there is no painter. A pressed row shows the Material ripple.
platformNotes: As on iOS, the whole row is the touch target, a button with onOpen or a link opened through LocalUriHandler otherwise (the web opens a new tab from the title). The web's messages object is one labels value with lambdas for the counted strings. Sources come from the conversation model; MonarchAiSourceListItem adds the web's used and snippet fields, and sources(message) gives a message's sources in first-appearance order. iOS uses isUsed, isNumbered and isInitiallyExpanded; Android drops the is prefix, as Material 3 does. The favicon field of a source is an address; Monarch loads no images, so the app passes painters through favicon, and a source without one shows a letter tile instead of the web's kind glyph. The parity map names collapsible, but only the sources after the first few are hidden, so the toggle is a ghost MonarchButton under the list rather than a MonarchCollapsible header. iOS's opensSource hint is the tap action name openSource here, because TalkBack reads it as "double tap to open the source".
accessibility: The list heading and the Used and Considered headings are headings.
Each source is one element read as "Source 1: title", then host, product and kind, then the snippet; with numbered false the number is left out.
A row that opens is a button at least 48dp high whose tap action is read as "open the source".
The favicon is decorative and hidden.
The toggle is a separate button whose text says Show all 5 sources or Show fewer.
edgeCases: Unsafe addresses such as javascript: are never opened; the row becomes plain text unless onOpen is given.
The group headings count every source, also the ones hidden while collapsed; a group with no source shown while collapsed has no heading.
collapseAfter 0 hides every source until the list is expanded.
Long titles and meta lines wrap; snippets stop at two lines with an ellipsis.
An empty list shows only the heading; leave the list out when a reply has no sources.

examples.template:
MonarchAiSourceList(
    items = listOf(
        MonarchAiSourceListItem(MonarchAiSourcePart(id = {{sources.0.id}}, title = {{sources.0.title}}, url = {{sources.0.url}}, kind = MonarchAiSourceKind.{{sources.0.kind|pascal}}, product = {{sources.0.product}}), snippet = {{sources.0.snippet}}),
        MonarchAiSourceListItem(MonarchAiSourcePart(id = {{sources.1.id}}, title = {{sources.1.title}}, url = {{sources.1.url}}, kind = MonarchAiSourceKind.{{sources.1.kind|pascal}}), snippet = {{sources.1.snippet}}),
        MonarchAiSourceListItem(MonarchAiSourcePart(id = {{sources.2.id}}, title = {{sources.2.title}}, kind = MonarchAiSourceKind.{{sources.2.kind|pascal}}, product = {{sources.2.product}}), used = {{sources.2.used}}),
        MonarchAiSourceListItem(MonarchAiSourcePart(id = {{sources.3.id}}, title = {{sources.3.title}}, kind = MonarchAiSourceKind.{{sources.3.kind|pascal}}), used = {{sources.3.used}}, snippet = {{sources.3.snippet}}),
    ),
    onOpen = {},
)

MonarchAiSourceList(
    items = listOf(
        MonarchAiSourceListItem(MonarchAiSourcePart(id = "s1", title = "Team handbook", url = "https://example.com/handbook", kind = MonarchAiSourceKind.Doc, product = "Docs"), snippet = "Requests are answered within two working days."),
        MonarchAiSourceListItem(MonarchAiSourcePart(id = "s2", title = "Support policy", url = "https://example.com/support-policy", kind = MonarchAiSourceKind.Web), snippet = "Urgent issues go to the on-call queue."),
        MonarchAiSourceListItem(MonarchAiSourcePart(id = "s3", title = "Ticket 1042", kind = MonarchAiSourceKind.Record, product = "Helpdesk"), used = false),
        MonarchAiSourceListItem(MonarchAiSourcePart(id = "s4", title = "Onboarding checklist.pdf", kind = MonarchAiSourceKind.File), used = false, snippet = "A list of first-week tasks."),
    ),
    onOpen = {},
)

examples.title: Sources read from a message, as links
examples.code:
val message = MonarchAiConversationMessage(
    id = "a1",
    role = MonarchAiRole.Assistant,
    parts = listOf(
        MonarchAiTextPart("Revenue grew 12%."),
        MonarchAiSourcePart("s1", "Q3 revenue report", "https://example.com/q3", MonarchAiSourceKind.Doc),
    ),
    createdAt = "2025-03-10T12:00:00.000Z",
)
MonarchAiSourceList(items = MonarchAiSourceListItem.sources(message), collapseAfter = null)
